I wrote `email?(string)` in `email.rb`. I haven't run it.

```ruby
def email?(string)
  string.match?(/\A[^@\s]+@[^@\s]+\.[^@\s]+\z/)
end
```

It returns true when the string has one `@`, some text before it, and a domain after it that contains a dot. Whitespace isn't allowed anywhere. This is a loose "looks like an email" check, not full RFC 5322 validation, so a few odd strings like `a@b..c` will still pass.
